item.title: From Microscopic Complementary Closure to Macroscopic Binary Coarse-Graining: A Quantum–Binary Multilevel Observation and Dual-Projection Hypothesis
item.description: This work proposes a conceptual framework for connecting quantum closure structures, local observation, fine-grained binary records, and conventional binary coarse-graining. At the binary level, the framework introduces a structural representation distinct from ordinary ordered binary notation. The states 00, 11, and \{01,10\} are first grouped into three basic relational classes. Adding a positive/reverse distinction produces six states. Assigning one of four source labels, A, B, C, or D, to each of the two binary positions further generates 3\times2\times4\times4=96 labeled structural states. item.title: A Falsifiable Closure Hypothesis Beneath Binary Quantum Readout: Two-Face Pairing, Eight Configurations, and Staged Experimental Protocols
item.description: This conservative preprint formalizes a candidate directional closure structure beneath ordinary binary quantum readout. A handwritten sixteen-face table is transcribed into eight complementary closure pairs: at each of four ordered slots, the paired faces preserve the direction label and complement the binary value. The accompanying inversion audit shows that a single value-plus-direction label, such as 0_A, does not uniquely reconstruct a closure pair; a second independent readout or a frozen dynamical rule is required. item.title: DCR Open Validation Request: Three-Channel Cross-Intervention Model Separation
item.description: An open preregistration and reproducibility package for testing whether a constrained three-reservoir exchange model predicts a held-out recovery intervention better than registered standard competing models. The package contains the preregistered three-channel protocol, data dictionary, statistical analysis plan, competing-model definitions, reproducibility code, automated tests, and file-integrity checks. This package does not claim new particles, sub-quantum constituents, or physics beyond standard quantum theory. Its purpose is to enable an independent, falsifiable test of whether a mechanism-sensitive third observation channel improves cross-intervention model separation relative to registered standard alternatives.

item.title: Exponential Quantum Advantage in Clock-Free Generation of Recursive Temporal Words
item.description: This record provides the complete reproducibility and audit archive for the manuscript "Exponential Quantum Advantage in Clock-Free Generation of Recursive Temporal Words." It contains the manuscript, supplemental material, certified classical and quantum bounds, independent verification code, figures, numerical outputs, and integrity data. The result establishes a standard quantum-information separation for clock-free generation of recursive temporal words. It does not claim subquantum structure, QEM-8 confirmation, or experimental validation.

item.title: Exact Sign-Sector Probabilities for the Diagonal of a Haar-Random Rotation in SO(3)
item.description: Let R be a Haar-random rotation matrix in SO(3). We determine the exact probabilities of the eight sign sectors defined by the diagonal entries (R_{11},R_{22},R_{33}). Each sign sector containing an even number of negative diagonal entries has probability 5/24, while each sector containing an odd number of negative diagonal entries has probability 1/24. Consequently, the total probability of the four even-parity sectors is 5/6, and the total probability of the four odd-parity sectors is 1/6. Two independent analytic derivations are presented. The first uses the unit-quaternion representation of Haar-random rotations together with Hopf-coordinate integration. item.title: Recursive Binary Words as Dimension-Bounded Temporal Memory Witnesses
item.description: Reproducibility archive for exact deterministic memory complexity and certified equal-dimension classical-quantum temporal separations for finite Thue-Morse words under a stationary, clock-free generation model. The archive contains source code, exact and interval certificates, machine-readable outputs, figures, manuscript source, and the compiled manuscript. The results are trusted-dimension temporal-memory witnesses; they are not device-independent statements, do not establish hidden quantum states, and do not modify standard finite-dimensional quantum theory. Source code is released under the MIT License; manuscript materials are released under CC BY 4.0.

item.title: A Forward Hypothesis of Recursive Closed Internal Structure Beneath Observable Binary States
item.description: 本文提出一种待验证的正向物理假设:外显二元状态0和1可能并非最终基本状态,而分别由方向相反的内部闭合关系01与10所生成。这里的01和10不被视为普通二进制字符串,而被视为具有顺序、方向、反演与闭合性质的不可约关系单元。 本文在暂时假定该假设成立的前提下,推导其可能产生的直接后果,包括同一外显状态下的内部差异、路径历史保留、内部反演、特征频率以及0/1镜像结构。进一步提出三种候选物理实现:方向—相位模型、概率流模型和闭合能量模型,并给出相应的正向实验验证路线,包括多路径相位实验、低功率弱谱学、内部反演搜索以及多类观测的联合检验。 本文不声称该假设已经获得实验确认,也不将三种候选模型视为最终物理结论。其目的在于把源于手稿的结构直觉转换为一个可计算、可证伪、可独立复现并可交由实验团队验证的研究框架,同时公开邀请具备量子控制、谱学、弱测量和多态读出能力的研究团队开展独立验证。 英文描述 This work proposes a falsifiable forward hypothesis that observable binary states 0 and 1 may not be fundamental, but may instead arise from oppositely oriented internal closed relations denoted as 01 and 10. item.title: A Binary-Observable, Quaternary-Closure Hypothesis for Quantum Systems: Formal Model, Operational-Equivalence Boundary, Simulation Audit, and Open Experimental Tests

item.title: Platform Integral as a Cross-System Mechanism for Window Formation in Hybrid Mode Systems
item.description: Stable transmission or propagation windows are widely observed in hybrid mode systems, including polaritonic and photonic crystal structures. Conventional interpretations attribute these windows to local extrema, such as minimum residue or maximum group index. item.title: Platform Integral Predicts Slow-Light Window Formation in Photonic Crystal Waveguides
item.description: Slow-light phenomena in photonic crystal waveguides are commonly characterized by large group index values near band edges. item.title: Protocol-Dependent Optimality in Near-Edge Systems: A Unified Explanation for Experimental Discrepancies in Slow-Light Regimes
item.description: This work presents a unified framework for understanding optimal operating points in near-edge physical systems, with a focus on slow-light photonic crystal waveguides.   By introducing a Difference Explanation Model (DEM), we show that system performance can be described as a balance between enhancement (gain) and degradation (loss), where the latter is strongly influenced by experimental protocols such as coupling configuration, polarization, and mode selection.   The framework explains why similar structures can exhibit significantly different optimal operating points, and provides a predictive expression for the shift of the optimal point under different protocols. item.title: Structure-Aware Spectral Reconstruction via Observation Window Compensation
item.description: This work presents a structure-aware reconstruction framework for recovering suppressed high-order components under observation window distortion. In many imaging and signal acquisition systems, the observation process acts as a non-uniform filter that attenuates specific structural components, leading to incomplete or biased reconstruction. We model the observation process as a weighted projection over structural components and introduce a window compensation approach to invert such distortions. By estimating the observation window and applying component-wise correction, the proposed method enables recovery of hidden structural information that is otherwise inaccessible from single observations. item.title: A Structural Generative Control Framework: Behavior Mode Generation under Structural Constraints
item.description: This work proposes a Structural Generative Control Framework (SGCF), a novel control paradigm in which control is formulated as behavior generation under structural constraints rather than direct action computation. Unlike traditional approaches such as PID, MPC, and reinforcement learning, which map system states directly to control actions, SGCF introduces an intermediate behavioral layer defined by a finite set of behavior modes. These modes emerge as stable solutions of an underlying structure composed of driving forces, relational constraints, and system limitations. item.title: From Structure to Behavior: Role-Semantic Invariants as the Basis of Behavioral Mode Generation
item.description: We propose a theoretical framework for behavior generation in dynamical systems, termed Structure-Constrained Behavior Generation (SCBG).   Unlike conventional approaches in control and learning, where behavior is derived from optimization or learned policies, SCBG suggests that behavior emerges as a constrained selection process defined by structural invariants.   A key contribution of this work is the introduction of role-semantic structural invariants, which extend traditional graph-based representations by incorporating functional roles associated with nodes and pathways. Within this framework, behavior is determined not by raw connectivity or parameter values, but by invariant structural relations including opposition, closure, hierarchical pathways, and role semantics. &nbs

item.title: Structure-Constrained Behavior Generation: Minimal Evidence for Structure-Dominant Behavioral Dynamics
item.description: We propose a minimal framework for behavior generation in dynamical systems, termed Structure-Constrained Behavior Generation (SCBG).   Unlike traditional control paradigms where behavior is derived from optimization or learned policies, SCBG suggests that behavior emerges as a selection from a structure-constrained set of reachable modes.   We construct a minimal 2D agent model with fixed local update rules and compare multiple structural configurations. item.title: Defect–Fiber Spectral Geometry and Cosmological Freeze-Out: A Unified Framework for Higgs, Flavor, and Neutrino Structure
item.description: This work presents a defect-fiber unified framework in which the Higgs sector, flavor hierarchies, neutrino suppression, and cosmological freeze-out are interpreted as low-energy readouts of a discrete spectral structure supported on cosmological defects.   The framework is built from a temperature-dependent order-parameter field generating defects whose worldvolume carries an internal asymmetric fiber. item.description: This work proposes a unified low-mode field framework describing critical mode mixing, slow-mode formation, and family structure generation across different physical systems.   The theory is formulated using a mother field defined on an extended manifold with an internal compact geometry. item.title: AI-Driven Mining of Traditional Chinese Medicine Classics for Discovery of Next-Generation Artemisinin-Class Natural Medicines
item.description: This research proposes an innovative drug discovery route: TCM ancient books → AI pattern analysis → potent drug clues → modern experimental verification. Based on the core signals of “single herb, remarkable efficacy, fresh use, low-temperature extraction” in ancient medical classics, we screened out three high-value medicinal plants: Pulsatilla chinensis, Paris polyphylla, and Hedyotis diffusa. AI virtual verification confirmed that all of them contain thermolabile active ingredients with significant antibacterial, anti-inflammatory, and anti-tumor activities. This study proves that TCM classics are a strategic treasure trove for global innovative drug research and development.
